keyFindings.description: The SyntaxError/z.ZodError test is applied around the whole of restoreRole(), which is not only a file read: restoreRole calls client.setRole (:558-563), and the real client parses the listener's answer — InterestWireSchema.parse(JSON.parse(raw)) at packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts:395, and an unguarded JSON.parse(error.details.responseBody) at :390 on a 409. A listener answering with something that is not JSON (a proxy's HTML 502, a truncated body) throws SyntaxError, and one whose JSON misses the schema throws ZodError; both are classified as a permanently unparseable role file, so nothing is queued, heldRole stays unset, no heartbeat retries, and the stderr line says 'the session starts without one' about a role file that was good. That is round two's finding still open for the most ordinary transient listener failure there is. Remedy: decide 'these bytes will never parse' inside readPersistedRole (session-identity.ts:61-69), the only place that knows the error came from the file, and return it as an outcome rather than letting the exception type stand in for its origin.

The inverse, and new in this delta: a role file failing with EACCES, EISDIR or ENOTDIR is now queued, and restoreRole throws on it every tick. transferRole sits before syncRegisteredInterests() in the heartbeat's serialized block, so that reconciliation never runs again — what a resumed session whose startup interests read failed depends on to adopt its subscriptions (tests/envoy-channel-registry.test.ts:328-365), and what clears a registry-side unsubscribe that failed (envoy-channel-server.ts:473-480, registry test :215-277). Before this delta those errors were logged and not queued, so the heartbeat still reached the reconciliation. The heartbeat does not hot-loop and recovers if the file is repaired or removed. One remedy serves both findings: classify at the parsing boundary, queue every other failure, and keep a queued role retry from skipping syncRegisteredInterests.

fixesVerified: Fix 1, the queued retry itself: a failed or refused listener request is queued as a transfer from the session's own id, transferRole clears the queue only once restoreRole resolves, so a repeated failure stays queued. Correct as far as it goes — the two findings above are its classification, not its retry.

Fix 2, refreshRoleRecord: the touch sits at the confirmed-holder return of reassertRole (:628), where 'still holding' is known, and touchStateFile is an utimes rather than a rewrite, so roles/ gains no temporary file every heartbeat. The failure latch reports once per failure run and retries every tick.
Fix 3, MD_VIEWPORT_QUERY is (min-width: 48rem) against Tailwind's --breakpoint-md: 48rem; COMPACT_ and PHONE_ left alone as asked.

Fix 4, the sweep's self-exclusion: roleStateFile(stateDirectory, currentSessionId) and pruneStateDirectory's join(directory, entry) build the same string, so the comparison holds; a record keyed by the running session survives its own startup sweep and is swept by the next session once that one is gone.

z.ZodError discrimination does work where the error really is the role file: zod 4.3.6 is pinned, classic .parse throws ZodRealError but both constructors carry the ZodError trait and zod's Symbol.hasInstance checks the trait, so instanceof holds. The defect is the origin of the exception, not the test itself.

The rewrite d4de531733a9 of 39175757c326: same parent 898037479328, byte-identical message, empty diff between the two, and the author corrected from the review App to the implement App. Every commit above main now carries its own role's App in both columns, checked with the default-branch read.
